overall.summary: Almost every number, threshold, shape and subgroup reproduces; refuted only on the number word 'most states' have no edge (31 of 51 states do have one), with minor weakenings: a second strong interaction (voice-mail plan by day use) left out of 'the one interaction', a 'daytime' detector that is also driven by evening use, one unit misdescribed as single-state, and two double-rounded AUCs.

findings.evidence: 20 of the 51 state indicators have no edge (null nodes -6,-7,-10,-11,-12,-17,-19 to -24,-32,-36,-37,-38,-44,-47,-49,-51); 31 states do have an edge (3 in state35_chain, 1 in state11_units, 5 in other_state_units, 22 in state_direct_linear). 'Most states' is wrong: a minority (39%) are ignored. The other inputs named (vmail messages -58, eve calls -63, night charge -67, intl charge -70) are correctly null.

findings.statement: heavy use also moves the calls threshold up, the one interaction in the model
findings.check: probe day minutes with and without a voice-mail plan (typical customer, day charge moved with day minutes)
findings.evidence: The voice-mail plan gates the heavy-use detector: at 150 day minutes the risk is 1.5% with or without the plan, at 300 minutes 99.9% without and 0.4% with it. That is a strong plan-by-day-use interaction (and day by evening use inside unit 469), so the calls-by-heavy-use effect is not the only interaction. The calls effect itself reproduces (at 270 min, no plan: 52.7% at 0 calls, 50.9% at 4, 71.2% at 5).
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/long_run/explanations/lr-72c47.json --set 'total day minutes=300' --set 'total day charge=51' --set 'voice mail plan=0|1' --nodes 469

findings.statement: The joint effect inside the model is heavy use with customer-service calls, within usage_service_calls
findings.evidence: Correct as far as it goes, but the heavy-use detector is itself a joint effect of day use, evening use and the voice-mail plan (risk at 300 day minutes: 99.9% without a plan, 0.4% with one; 1.5% for both at 150 minutes).

findings.evidence: directions and shapes reproduce

usage_service_calls.why: The service-calls hinge (flat to two calls, steep from three) and the heavy-use-without-voice-mail detector are confirmed, but the detector is a day-plus-evening load (124 of its 360 customers have under 250 day minutes) and the stated concept explains r2 0.63.

state35_chain.why: Confirmed as three small state offsets (New Jersey up, Alaska and Ohio down) whose large internal terms cancel; a geographic reading, though only a fitted lookup.

state11_units.why: Hawaii customers get a much lower score (0.1% vs 1.1% typical), matching their 4.1% churn rate; the indicator explains the exit fully.

other_state_units.why: Per-state offsets dominated by Vermont (exit -2.56), confirmed by probe; the concept explains 0.83.

eve_night_hinges.why: The evening-charge hinge (off below about $12, then lowering risk) is confirmed, but the night-calls hinge is outside the reading (concept 0.68).

tenure_hinge.why: Accounts older than about 85 days get a slowly rising score, a single-input hinge fully read as account length.

area_code_offsets.why: Area code barely matters (1.1% to 1.2%, AUC unchanged); the reading 'nearly unused' is confirmed.

plan_and_calls_linear.why: An international plan raises risk and more international calls lower it, confirmed by probe and by the plan holders' 42.4% churn rate.

state_direct_linear.why: A table of 22 per-state offsets with no common reading (best concept 0.20); only its extremes are named.
